q: What does "the ball is in your court" mean?
h: The idea comes from tennis: now you must hit it back.

q: What does it mean to "hit the nail on the head"?
h: Like a perfect hammer blow, you got it just right.

q: A day on Mars is only a little longer than a day on Earth.
h: A Martian day, called a sol, lasts about 24 h 40 min.

q: Sharks existed on Earth before trees did.
h: Sharks are over 400 million years old; trees came later.

q: Oxford University is older than the Aztec Empire.
h: Teaching at Oxford began by 1096; Tenochtitlan rose in 1325.

q: Bananas are slightly radioactive.
h: They contain potassium-40, but the dose is tiny.

q: A group of owls can be called a "parliament".
h: Like a "murder" of crows, it's a playful group name.

q: Your stomach replaces its inner lining every few days.
h: Fresh cells stop the stomach's acid from digesting you.

q: Sea otters have the thickest fur of any animal.
h: Up to about 1 million hairs per square inch (6.5 cm²).

q: The Pacific Ocean is larger than all of Earth's land put together.
h: It covers about a third of the whole planet's surface.

q: A newborn baby has more bones than an adult.
h: Babies have around 300 bones; many fuse as we grow.

q: Antarctica is the largest desert in the world.
h: A desert is defined by low rain or snow, not by heat.

q: Ordinary window glass is made mainly from sand.
h: Sand is melted with soda ash and lime to make glass.

q: Pure water is actually a poor conductor of electricity.
h: Dissolved salts and minerals carry the current, not water.

q: Dogs see only in black and white.
h: Dogs see blues and yellows but struggle with red and green.

q: Toilets flush in the opposite direction south of the equator.
h: The Earth's spin is far too weak to steer a toilet bowl.

q: Shaving makes hair grow back thicker.
h: Cut hair has a blunt tip, so it just feels coarser.

q: Camels store water in their humps.
h: The humps store fat, which camels can use for energy.

q: You lose most of your body heat through your head.
h: Heat escapes from any uncovered skin, not mainly the head.

q: Chameleons change color mainly to blend into their background.
h: They change mostly to signal mood and control temperature.

q: A coin dropped from a skyscraper could kill a person below.
h: Air resistance keeps a falling coin to a harmless speed.

q: Viking warriors wore horned helmets into battle.
h: Horned helmets come from 1800s stage costumes.

q: Eating sugar makes children hyperactive.
h: Careful blind studies have found no such effect.

q: The Moon gives off its own light.
h: Moonlight is sunlight reflected off the Moon's surface.
